vetted vs PyRadiomics 3.0.1 GLDM on the compat phantom (bench_compat_liver_3d, label 1), recipe gldm3d.pyradiomics_bincount20. Nyxus' GLDM_GREYDEPTH=-20 and PyRadiomics' binCount=20 produce the same twenty levels; both sides walk the full 26-voxel neighbourhood at Chebyshev distance 1 with the dependence cutoff alpha=0, and both start the dependence count at 1 so a voxel with no dependent neighbour lands in the same column. No convention separates them, which is why SPEC 7's exact tier applies: the measured residual is at most 7.11e-15 ABSOLUTE (3GLDM_SDHGLE) and 8.79e-16 relative across the thirteen features that take no logarithm, eight of them exactly 0, asserted with ASSERT_NEAR at abs=1e-9. Backed by THE FOURTEEN SCALARS AND THE MATRIX THEY CONTRACT: all fourteen are sums over one P(i,j) dependence matrix, so TEST_3D_GLDM_MATRIX_PYRADIOMICS pins that matrix too - all 163 non-empty cells, its Ng/Nd/Nz/Np, and the count of populated cells - against PyRadiomics' own P_gldm array, read through its ivector AND jvector because PyRadiomics deletes the rows of absent grey levels and the columns of absent dependences. Nz == Np is asserted from the cube rather than the matrix, which is what says Nyxus counts no voxel outside the ROI into the matrix. The assertion reads the cube the same extraction produced, so perturbing one voxel of it fails. TEST_3D_GLDM_SMALLMATRIX_PYRADIOMICS runs the same assertion on a 4x4x3 volume whose two populated slices are identical, forcing every dependence to 2*(in-slice matches)+2 - the direct check that the neighbourhood includes the z offsets. The generator rebuilds the matrix from the definition independently of PyRadiomics' C extension and requires all 163 cells to agree. test_3d_gldm_regression.h pins Nyxus' own values on the ut phantom at recipe gldm3d.regression_ut_phantom and claims no oracle. Evidence: tests/vetting/audit/gldm_3d_pyradiomics_vetting_report.md, generator tests/vetting/oracles/gen_gldm3d_pyradiomics.py. 3GLDM_DE is the exception at abs=4e-3: it is the family's only sum over logarithms and Nyxus takes it through fast_log10(), a float-precision approximation divided by a ten-digit LOG10_2, where PyRadiomics uses numpy.log2. Measured residual 1.7512e-3 absolute / 2.65e-4 relative (Nyxus 6.6031219389041276 against PyRadiomics 6.6048731874541904); the band is that doubled and rounded up to one significant figure. A documented fast path, banded rather than reported. Note the 2D twin's identical calc_DE() measures 1.3e-3 RELATIVE, five times wider, so this figure is this family's own and not carried across. Neither matrix case is named in test_name: TEST_NYXUS.TEST_3D_GLDM_MATRIX_PYRADIOMICS asserts the cells of P rather than this feature's value, and TEST_NYXUS.TEST_3D_GLDM_SMALLMATRIX_PYRADIOMICS asserts them on a hand-written unbinned 4x4x3 volume that is not this row's benchmark and not this row's recipe. Both are corroboration for the recipe, recorded here; test_name keeps the one case that asserts the value this row claims.

Defect guard, recipe gldm3d.regression_constant_roi (bench_constant_roi_3d, GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0); establishes no vetting (SPEC 1) and endorses nothing. A NONEMPTY ROI OF ONE INTENSITY comes back as the configured no-value sentinel for all fourteen features -- production defaults it to 0.0 (ResultOptions::noval_), a value several of the fourteen also compute legitimately. D3_GLDM_feature::calculate()'s aux_min == aux_max intercept emits it -- written for BLANK ROIs, but tested on the intensity extrema. THE ARITHMETIC UNDER THE INTERCEPT IS NOT WRONG: restricting the intercept to empty cubes as a negative control, at this recipe's GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, Nyxus reproduces PyRadiomics on all seven dependence-axis features to the last bit (SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DN 15.333333333333334, DNN 0.31944444444444442, DV 26.743055555555554, GLN 48, GLV 0), 3GLDM_DE differs by the family's documented fast_log10 residual, and the grey-level features differ only because no-binning keeps the raw intensity 7 as the level where binWidth=1 maps it to 1. The intercept is the whole defect. A fix is still not one line: at radiomics binning TextureFeature::to_grayscale_radiomix() computes binW = (max - min) / binCount, zero here, so every voxel bins to background and the Nz == 0 branch emits the same sentinel by a second route -- and that route divides by zero and converts NaN to PixIntens, which the intercept is what keeps unreachable. That is why this cell is asserted at GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, where the intercept stands alone. The case runs under a sentinel of -98765.0 so a pass says the intercept fired rather than the features happening to compute zero. Such an ROI is reachable wherever a segmentation lands on a flat or saturated region, and its dependence matrix is well defined: PyRadiomics 3.0.1 computes it on the same 4x4x3 voxels at binWidth=1, gldm_a=0, distances=[1] -- P_gldm 1x4 = [8, 20, 16, 4] over one grey level, SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DE 1.7841591278514204, GLN 48. So this is a divergence Nyxus owns, not a convention difference. It is guarded rather than fixed here because the same intercept is shared by 3d_gldzm, 3d_glszm, 3d_ngldm, 3d_ngtdm and their 2D twins, so changing it moves production output well beyond this family. Evidence: tests/vetting/matrix/gldm3d.md.

Defect guard, recipe gldm3d.regression_constant_roi (bench_constant_roi_3d, GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0); establishes no vetting (SPEC 1) and endorses nothing. A NONEMPTY ROI OF ONE INTENSITY comes back as the configured no-value sentinel for all fourteen features -- production defaults it to 0.0 (ResultOptions::noval_), a value several of the fourteen also compute legitimately. D3_GLDM_feature::calculate()'s aux_min == aux_max intercept emits it -- written for BLANK ROIs, but tested on the intensity extrema. THE ARITHMETIC UNDER THE INTERCEPT IS NOT WRONG: restricting the intercept to empty cubes as a negative control, at this recipe's GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, Nyxus reproduces PyRadiomics on all seven dependence-axis features to the last bit (SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DN 15.333333333333334, DNN 0.31944444444444442, DV 26.743055555555554, GLN 48, GLV 0), 3GLDM_DE differs by the family's documented fast_log10 residual, and the grey-level features differ only because no-binning keeps the raw intensity 7 as the level where binWidth=1 maps it to 1. The intercept is the whole defect. A fix is still not one line: at radiomics binning TextureFeature::to_grayscale_radiomix() computes binW = (max - min) / binCount, zero here, so every voxel bins to background and the Nz == 0 branch emits the same sentinel by a second route -- and that route divides by zero and converts NaN to PixIntens, which the intercept is what keeps unreachable. That is why this cell is asserted at GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, where the intercept stands alone. The case runs under a sentinel of -98765.0 so a pass says the intercept fired rather than the features happening to compute zero. Such an ROI is reachable wherever a segmentation lands on a flat or saturated region, and its dependence matrix is well defined: PyRadiomics 3.0.1 computes it on the same 4x4x3 voxels at binWidth=1, gldm_a=0, distances=[1] -- P_gldm 1x4 = [8, 20, 16, 4] over one grey level, SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DE 1.7841591278514204, GLN 48. So this is a divergence Nyxus owns, not a convention difference. It is guarded rather than fixed here because the same intercept is shared by 3d_gldzm, 3d_glszm, 3d_ngldm, 3d_ngtdm and their 2D twins, so changing it moves production output well beyond this family. Evidence: tests/vetting/matrix/gldm3d.md.

vetted vs PyRadiomics 3.0.1 GLDM on the compat phantom (bench_compat_liver_3d, label 1), recipe gldm3d.pyradiomics_bincount20. Nyxus' GLDM_GREYDEPTH=-20 and PyRadiomics' binCount=20 produce the same twenty levels; both sides walk the full 26-voxel neighbourhood at Chebyshev distance 1 with the dependence cutoff alpha=0, and both start the dependence count at 1 so a voxel with no dependent neighbour lands in the same column. No convention separates them, which is why SPEC 7's exact tier applies: the measured residual is at most 7.11e-15 ABSOLUTE (3GLDM_SDHGLE) and 8.79e-16 relative across the thirteen features that take no logarithm, eight of them exactly 0, asserted with ASSERT_NEAR at abs=1e-9. Backed by THE FOURTEEN SCALARS AND THE MATRIX THEY CONTRACT: all fourteen are sums over one P(i,j) dependence matrix, so TEST_3D_GLDM_MATRIX_PYRADIOMICS pins that matrix too - all 163 non-empty cells, its Ng/Nd/Nz/Np, and the count of populated cells - against PyRadiomics' own P_gldm array, read through its ivector AND jvector because PyRadiomics deletes the rows of absent grey levels and the columns of absent dependences. Nz == Np is asserted from the cube rather than the matrix, which is what says Nyxus counts no voxel outside the ROI into the matrix. The assertion reads the cube the same extraction produced, so perturbing one voxel of it fails. TEST_3D_GLDM_SMALLMATRIX_PYRADIOMICS runs the same assertion on a 4x4x3 volume whose two populated slices are identical, forcing every dependence to 2*(in-slice matches)+2 - the direct check that the neighbourhood includes the z offsets. The generator rebuilds the matrix from the definition independently of PyRadiomics' C extension and requires all 163 cells to agree. test_3d_gldm_regression.h pins Nyxus' own values on the ut phantom at recipe gldm3d.regression_ut_phantom and claims no oracle. Evidence: tests/vetting/audit/gldm_3d_pyradiomics_vetting_report.md, generator tests/vetting/oracles/gen_gldm3d_pyradiomics.py. Neither matrix case is named in test_name: TEST_NYXUS.TEST_3D_GLDM_MATRIX_PYRADIOMICS asserts the cells of P rather than this feature's value, and TEST_NYXUS.TEST_3D_GLDM_SMALLMATRIX_PYRADIOMICS asserts them on a hand-written unbinned 4x4x3 volume that is not this row's benchmark and not this row's recipe. Both are corroboration for the recipe, recorded here; test_name keeps the one case that asserts the value this row claims.

Every run that does not pass that option computes this family here, and IBSI=true reaches the same code path by forcing greyInfo=0. Under SPEC 5.1 that is VALID-BUT-PRODUCTION-ONLY, which is a regression row. The gldm3d.regression_ut_phantom pins cannot stand in for it: on the same ROI the two configurations differ by orders of magnitude (3GLDM_HGLE 4275550.79 against 1957.19, 3GLDM_SDE 0.86996 against 0.15361, 3GLDM_GLV 341996.30 against 153.09), so a pin taken at 64 guards nothing at 0. GREYDEPTH is inert for this family and is held at the neighbouring recipe's 64 so the two tables differ in the one setting under test. No oracle claim: whether PyRadiomics can be made to skip discretisation on a non-integer intensity volume has not been answered. Pins regenerated at %.17g by test_3d_gldm_dump_nobinning_regression(). Defect guard, recipe gldm3d.regression_constant_roi (bench_constant_roi_3d, GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0); establishes no vetting (SPEC 1) and endorses nothing. A NONEMPTY ROI OF ONE INTENSITY comes back as the configured no-value sentinel for all fourteen features -- production defaults it to 0.0 (ResultOptions::noval_), a value several of the fourteen also compute legitimately. D3_GLDM_feature::calculate()'s aux_min == aux_max intercept emits it -- written for BLANK ROIs, but tested on the intensity extrema. THE ARITHMETIC UNDER THE INTERCEPT IS NOT WRONG: restricting the intercept to empty cubes as a negative control, at this recipe's GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, Nyxus reproduces PyRadiomics on all seven dependence-axis features to the last bit (SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DN 15.333333333333334, DNN 0.31944444444444442, DV 26.743055555555554, GLN 48, GLV 0), 3GLDM_DE differs by the family's documented fast_log10 residual, and the grey-level features differ only because no-binning keeps the raw intensity 7 as the level where binWidth=1 maps it to 1. The intercept is the whole defect. A fix is still not one line: at radiomics binning TextureFeature::to_grayscale_radiomix() computes binW = (max - min) / binCount, zero here, so every voxel bins to background and the Nz == 0 branch emits the same sentinel by a second route -- and that route divides by zero and converts NaN to PixIntens, which the intercept is what keeps unreachable. That is why this cell is asserted at GLDM_GREYDEPTH=0, where the intercept stands alone. The case runs under a sentinel of -98765.0 so a pass says the intercept fired rather than the features happening to compute zero. Such an ROI is reachable wherever a segmentation lands on a flat or saturated region, and its dependence matrix is well defined: PyRadiomics 3.0.1 computes it on the same 4x4x3 voxels at binWidth=1, gldm_a=0, distances=[1] -- P_gldm 1x4 = [8, 20, 16, 4] over one grey level, SDE 0.0066408036122542298, LDE 239.41666666666666, DE 1.7841591278514204, GLN 48. So this is a divergence Nyxus owns, not a convention difference. It is guarded rather than fixed here because the same intercept is shared by 3d_gldzm, 3d_glszm, 3d_ngldm, 3d_ngtdm and their 2D twins, so changing it moves production output well beyond this family. Vetted against PyRadiomics 3.0.1 GLSZM on the compat phantom (bench_compat_liver_3d, label 1), recipe glszm3d.pyradiomics_bincount20. Nyxus' GLSZM_GREYDEPTH=-20 and PyRadiomics' binCount=20 produce the same twenty levels, and both sides gather zones over the full 26-voxel neighbourhood, so no convention separates them: the measured residual is within a few ULP (worst 1.19e-15) on fifteen of the sixteen features, asserted at rel=1e-9. 3GLSZM_ZE is the exception at rel=1e-3, its residual 1.9e-4, because Nyxus takes the only logarithm in the family through fast_log10() -- a documented fast path, banded rather than reported. Backed by the SIXTEEN SCALARS AND THE MATRIX THEY CONTRACT: test_3d_glszm_matrix_pyradiomics reads the size-zone matrix off the feature object calculate() filled -- all 186 non-empty cells of the 20x634 table, its Ng/Ns/Nz/Np, the width and height it was allocated at, and a count proving no cell outside them is populated -- against PyRadiomics' own P_glszm array, read through its jvector because PyRadiomics deletes the columns for zone sizes nothing occupies. A defect planted in the production fill loop alone fails it, naming the level and the size, while all sixteen scalars still pass. The family's other assertions are their own rows: glszm3d.pyradiomics_ibsi_gapped, glszm3d.regression_ut_phantom and glszm3d.regression_ut_phantom_nobinning. tests/python/test_nyxus.py::test_3d_glszm_compatibility asserts these same goldens through the Python API; neither is this row's assertion. Evidence: tests/vetting/audit/glszm_3d_pyradiomics_vetting_report.md; generator tests/vetting/oracles/gen_glszm3d_pyradiomics.py.

Vetted against PyRadiomics 3.0.1 GLSZM on bench_cube3_gapped_levels, recipe glszm3d.pyradiomics_ibsi_gapped: a 3x3x3 literal carrying grey levels 1, 3 and 5 with 2 and 4 absent, read by Nyxus at IBSI=true and by PyRadiomics at binWidth=1. This is the only configuration that reaches calculate()'s IBSI-only expressions -- row = zone.first-1 and Ng = max(I) -- and the only fixture on which they are distinguishable from the ones beside them, since a level's position and the level itself are different numbers here. Both sides report Ng = 5 for three occupied levels. Fifteen features agree exactly; 3GLSZM_ZE is banded at rel=2e-3 on a measured residual of 1.1e-3, the same fast_log10 path costing more on a six-zone matrix than on the phantom's 860. The size-zone matrix is pinned cell by cell off the feature object as well. test_3d_glszm_ibsi_equals_no_binning_mechanics measures that this configuration and GLSZM_GREYDEPTH=0 produce bit-identical values and matrices, which is why tests/vetting/matrix/glszm3d.md carries one cell for the two. Evidence: tests/vetting/audit/glszm_3d_pyradiomics_vetting_report.md.
